title: North Point Wet Weather Facility
description: Built in 1951, the North Point Wet Weather Facility treats excess stormwater during heavy rains—but its waterfront location near Fisherman’s Wharf leaves it vulnerable to flooding.

title: Embarcadero SAFE Navigation Center
description: This homeless shelter for 200 people is directly across the street from the bay’s shore. It could be inundated if sea levels rise 6.5 feet by 2100, which some scenarios predict if greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise.

title: I-80 Bay Bridge On-Ramp and Interchange
description: Sea level rise and storm surges can severely disrupt traffic. Several lanes in the complex of on-ramps leading to the Bay Bridge flooded in January 2026 after heavy rains and high King tides raised water levels 2.5 feet above normal.

title: Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport
description: OAK Airport has determined that it will be vulnerable to extreme storm surge flooding by 2050–so the airport recently spent $30 million to raise the height of the 4.5 mile dike surrounding the airport. More than 10 million passengers passed through the airport in 2025.

title: Palo Alto Horizontal Levee
description: The city of Palo Alto is building an innovative way to protect its Harbor Marsh from sea level rise, and treat city wastewater at the same time. It’s called a “horizontal levee”—a wide, gently sloping shoreline covered with native vegetation that can change and grow as sea level rises and filters waste water before it enters the Bay.

title: Suisun Marsh
description: This 85,000-acre marsh—California’s largest remaining coastal wetland—supports 200+ bird species, 43 mammals, and many fish. Rising seas may upset its vital balance of fresh and salty water the marsh ecosystem depends on.
